title: Junior Core Mathematics • Structured Problem-Solving Series (Set 42)
subject: Mathematics

questions.title: Question 1: Linear Inequality, Rational Linear Equation, Factorization & Transposition

parts.prompt: Solve the inequality: $$7 - 3x > x + 3$$, where $x$ is a real number. Illustrate your solution on a number line.
parts.hint: Collect all terms with x on one side: $7 - 3 > x + 3x$. Remember to reverse the inequality sign if you divide by a negative number.

parts.prompt:
Find the truth set of the rational equation:
$$\frac{2}{3}(2y - 1) - \frac{1}{3}(y + 4) = 1$$
parts.hint: Multiply through by 3 (the common denominator) to eliminate fractions, then expand and solve for y.
Group terms pairwise: $x(a + b) - y(a + b)$.
parts.workedSolution: $$ax + bx - ay - by = x(a + b) - y(a + b) = (a + b)(x - y)$$.

parts.prompt: Make $t$ the subject of the relation: $$v = u - gt$$.
parts.hint: Isolate the term containing t: $gt = u - v$, then divide by g.

questions.title: Question 2: Commercial Property Revenue, Taxes & Percentage Expenses

parts.prompt:
A property owner leased out an apartment building for $\text{GH¢ } 360,000.00$ per annum. During the year, she paid $15\%$ of the gross rent as income tax and $20\%$ of the gross rent as municipal property rates. She also spent $\text{GH¢ } 18,000.00$ on building repairs and maintenance.
Calculate the property owner's **total annual expenses**.
parts.hint: Find 15% of 360,000, 20% of 360,000, and add the repair expenses of 18,000.

parts.prompt: Calculate the net remainder of the rental income left after settling all total expenses.
parts.hint: Net remainder = Gross Rent - Total Expenses.

parts.prompt: Calculate the percentage of the gross rent that was spent on repairs and maintenance.
parts.hint: Percentage = (Amount spent on repairs / Gross Rent) × 100%.

parts.prompt:
Triangle $ABC$ has vertices $A(1, 1)$, $B(4, 3)$, and $C(2, 5)$ on the Cartesian plane shown above.
Write down the coordinates of the image vertices $A_1, B_1,$ and $C_1$ under a reflection in the $y$-axis (the line $x = 0$).
parts.hint: Reflection in y-axis maps $(x, y) \to (-x, y)$.

parts.prompt: Write down the coordinates of the image vertices $A_2, B_2,$ and $C_2$ under a reflection of triangle $ABC$ in the $x$-axis (the line $y = 0$).
Determine the single transformation that maps triangle $A_1B_1C_1$ directly onto triangle $A_2B_2C_2$.
parts.hint: Compare points: (-x, y) maps to (x, -y). Both coordinates change signs.
parts.workedSolution:
Notice that for corresponding vertices:
$$A_1(-1, 1) \to A_2(1, -1)$$
$$B_1(-4, 3) \to B_2(4, -3)$$
$$C_1(-2, 5) \to C_2(2, -5)$$
This mapping conforms to $$(x, y) \to (-x, -y)$$, which is a **rotation of $180^\circ$ about the origin $(0, 0)$** (or a reflection in the origin).

parts.prompt:
The frequency distribution table below shows the marks obtained out of $10$ by a class of $64$ pupils in a mental mathematics test:

| Mark ($x$) | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Frequency ($f$) | 9 | 14 | 13 | 10 | 5 | 8 | 2 | 3 |

(i) State the **modal mark** of the distribution.
(ii) Find the total number of pupils who scored more than $5\text{ marks}$.
(iii) Calculate the **mean mark** of the class, correct to two decimal places.
parts.hint: Mode is the mark with highest frequency. Mean = $\sum fx / \sum f$. Scores > 5 are 6, 7, 8, and 9.
parts.workedSolution:
**(i) Modal mark:**
The highest frequency is $14$, which corresponds to mark **3**.

**(ii) Pupils scoring > 5 marks:**
$$\text{Count} = f(6) + f(7) + f(8) + f(9) = 5 + 8 + 2 + 3 = 18\text{ pupils}$$

**(iii) Mean mark:**
$$\sum fx = (2 \times 9) + (3 \times 14) + (4 \times 13) + (5 \times 10) + (6 \times 5) + (7 \times 8) + (8 \times 2) + (9 \times 3)$$
$$\sum fx = 18 + 42 + 52 + 50 + 30 + 56 + 16 + 27 = 291$$
$$\text{Mean} = \frac{\sum fx}{\sum f} = \frac{291}{64} \approx 4.546875$$
Correct to two decimal places: **4.55 marks**.

parts.prompt:
If a pupil is chosen at random from this class:
(i) What is the probability that the pupil obtained exactly $7\text{ marks}$?
(ii) What is the probability that the pupil scored at most $3\text{ marks}$?
parts.hint: P(7 marks) = f(7) / 64. 'At most 3 marks' means marks 2 and 3: [f(2) + f(3)] / 64.
parts.workedSolution:
**(i) Probability of obtaining 7 marks:**
$$P(x = 7) = \frac{f(7)}{64} = \frac{8}{64} = \frac{1}{8}$$

**(ii) Probability of scoring at most 3 marks (marks 2 and 3):**
$$\text{Count} = f(2) + f(3) = 9 + 14 = 23$$
$$P(x \le 3) = \frac{23}{64}$$.

questions.title: Question 5: Geometric Compass Trapezium Construction & Diagonal Measurement
questions.diagramSvg: <svg viewBox='0 0 340 220' width='100%' height='200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><polygon points='40,170 240,170 240,57 140,57' fill='#f8fafc' stroke='#1e293b' stroke-width='2'/><rect x='222' y='152' width='18' height='18' fill='none' stroke='#1e293b' stroke-width='1.5'/><rect x='222' y='57' width='18' height='18' fill='none' stroke='#1e293b' stroke-width='1.5'/><line x1='40' y1='170' x2='240' y2='57' stroke='#2563eb' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='4'/><text x='25' y='180' font-size='12' font-weight='bold'>P</text><text x='250' y='180' font-size='12' font-weight='bold'>Q</text><text x='250' y='55' font-size='12' font-weight='bold'>R</text><text x='130' y='50' font-size='12' font-weight='bold'>S</text><text x='130' y='190' font-size='11'>|PQ| = 9 cm</text><text x='180' y='45' font-size='11'>SR || PQ</text><text x='70' y='125' font-size='11'>|PS| = 6.5 cm</text><text x='130' y='120' font-size='11' font-weight='bold' fill='#2563eb'>|PR| = ?</text><text x='65' y='165' font-size='10'>60°</text></svg>

parts.prompt:
In a geometric compass and ruler construction:
1. Construct line segment $|PQ| = 9\text{ cm}$.
2. At $Q$, construct a perpendicular line to $PQ$.
3. At $P$, construct angle $\angle QPS = 60^\circ$ such that $|PS| = 6.5\text{ cm}$.
4. Construct a line parallel to $PQ$ through $S$ to meet the perpendicular line from $Q$ at vertex $R$.
(i) State the geometric name of the quadrilateral $PQRS$.
(ii) Calculate the perpendicular height $|QR|$ using the sine ratio ($|QR| = |PS| \sin 60^\circ$, where $\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.866$).
parts.hint: A quadrilateral with one pair of opposite sides parallel and adjacent perpendicular angles is a right-angled trapezium. Height = 6.5 × 0.866.
parts.workedSolution:
**(i) Geometric classification:**
Since $SR \parallel PQ$ and $\angle PQR = 90^\circ$, quadrilateral $PQRS$ is a **right-angled trapezium**.

**(ii) Perpendicular height $|QR|$:**
$$|QR| = |PS| \times \sin 60^\circ = 6.5 \times 0.866 \approx 5.629\text{ cm}$$
Correct to two decimal places: **5.63 cm**.

parts.prompt: Calculate the diagonal length $|PR|$ using Pythagoras' theorem on right-angled triangle $PQR$, given base $|PQ| = 9\text{ cm}$ and height $|QR| = 5.63\text{ cm}$.
parts.workedSolution:
In right-angled $\Delta PQR$:
$$|PR|^2 = |PQ|^2 + |QR|^2$$
$$|PR|^2 = 9^2 + 5.63^2 = 81 + 31.6969 = 112.6969$$
$$|PR| = \sqrt{112.6969} \approx 10.6158\text{ cm}$$
Therefore, the length of diagonal $|PR|$ is **$10.62\text{ cm}$** (or approximately $10.6\text{ cm}$ by direct measurement).
